# the contributor independent audit: near-triangle quadrilateral extraction

Read candidate 39f4da3e2b2dd7eb
in full. PASS, no correction needed. The exact verifier reruns PASS8847.

Checked the outer-triangle geometry, corner fractions, and the labeling
which bounds the long fraction by51/100. The missing corner is one
closed-halfspace trace up to area zero, so its relative area is exactly
the normalized cap distance to the chosen containing triangle.

The low-cap classification includes every normal. A two-vertex cap has
the claimed complementary-product lower bound; a one-vertex cap's
coefficient sum and product force both coefficients into(29/20,31/20).
The supporting/vertex boundary cases follow by continuity, not deletion
of the boundary direction.

The point in Section3 is inside the actual quadrilateral. The same
original cap's coefficient bounds give losses at most(tau,0,tau/5)
for the three possible vertex types. Independently expanded all three
products, obtaining the displayed quadratic coefficients. The remaining
normals retain their fixed area gap after deletion. The resulting
finite inequality gives excess at least tau/45 with the stated cutoff.

The initial affine-neighborhood hypothesis is used constructively:
coordinate support vertices give an inscribed triangle of area at
least(1-12delta)/2, while the containing shifted triangle gives the
upper area bound. Their ratio yields h<=24delta. Any three actual
vertices of a genuine quadrilateral place the fourth beyond exactly
one of the inscribed triangle's edges; the final normalization and
endpoint exchange are legitimate arbitrary CONTINUOUS affine maps.
No lattice is transformed because the result is purely ordinary
planar geometry. No optimal comparison triangle is assumed to exist.

The total missing-area conclusion is stronger than the preceding
small-corner support theorem, but is explicitly limited to quadrilaterals.
It is not a theorem for arbitrary polygons, smooth bodies, or OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
